evidence.note: Started uvicorn and ran one health probe, but against a malformed address (127.0.0.0) with no confirmation of a good response; the only runtime endpoint check in the whole run.
Reasoned explicitly about the canary-strip SHA256 pinning rule but never ran shasum/sha256 to verify any of the three vendored libraries actually match the pinned digests.
Considered running the pytest gates to learn expected I/O but no pytest invocation ever occurs.
The bulk of 'verification' is grep/cat/sed inspection of its own source (oauth, timelines, create_status, admin scopes) — code reading, not runtime exercise of login/post/timeline flows.
Ends by killing the server; no persistence-across-restart test, no CSP/header curl, no scope-enforcement test, no offline-boot or time-compression check, and no anti-cheat probing anywhere.

reasoning: The agent ran the server and made a single (malformed) health check and seeded data, then verified everything else by reading its own source code with grep/cat rather than exercising it. It thought about hashes and pytest but never executed hash comparisons, header/CSP inspection, scope/persistence checks, or the anti-cheat conditions. That matches anchor 3 (ad hoc manual checks of a few endpoints with no verification of hashes, headers, scopes, persistence, or anti-cheat) and falls short of anchor 5's end-to-end flow exercise and offline/hash confirmation.
